reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification of every numbered line (blank lines 0002-0004, 0006-0007, 0010-0011, 0013-0014, 0016, 0022-0023, 0025, 0027, 0029, 0031, 0033, 0035, 0037, 0039, 0042-0045, 0047, 0050-0051, 0053-0055, 0057, 0059-0060, 0062-0064, 0075-0078 carry no content and are vacuously fine).
0001 Claim statement; acceptable as the target to be proved, though 'partitioned into sub-graphs' and 'pi is a part of P' are never made precise (how the local permutations glue into a global P is exactly the difficulty).
0005 Label 'Proof:'; no content.
0008 Announces an algorithmic proof; no content.
0009 Asserts the cost of finding P is polynomial in beta - this is the conclusion, stated here as a roadmap, so not yet a defect but nothing is justified.
0012 Cites [1] for Aut-generating-set construction being GI-complete (correct) and declares Luks's technique [2] 'can be used here'; the latter is a bare assertion - Luks's method is specific to bounded valence and no reduction to that setting is given. Hand-wave, load-bearing later.
0015 Notation heading; fine.
0017 Definition of M_(k,e), R_(k,e), S_(k,e); a legitimate definition.
0018-0021 Displayed block form of H; sloppy - the below-diagonal blocks are written R_(i,j) where the adjacency matrix requires R_(i,j)^T - but harmless notation, not a logical error.
0024 'Assume beta <= n^3': an extra hypothesis not present in the Claim, which is stated for arbitrary beta; it weakens what can be concluded but is at least explicit.
0030 Step 1 forms all direct products pi_1 x pi_2 with pi_i in beta_i; well defined, but note beta_i were introduced as maps taking G_i to H_i, while gamma_1 is said to act on H_1 ∪ H_2 - the direction is already confused.
0032 |beta_1||beta_2| < n^9: true but loose (n^3 * n^3 = n^6 under 0024); the claim that each element acts on H_1 ∪ H_2 is by construction.
0034 Step 2 heading; no content.
0036 Definition of alpha_1 imposing simultaneously M_(1,2)^pi = M_(1,2), R_(1,2)^pi = S_(1,2), H_1^pi = G_1, H_2^pi = G_2. These conditions are mutually inconsistent unless G and H are literally the same matrices: fixing M_(1,2) forces H_1^pi = H_1, so H_1^pi = G_1 demands G_1 = H_1 as matrices, not merely isomorphic. The set is generically empty.
0038 FIRST FAILING STEP: 'alpha_1 is the set of automorphisms of matrix M_(1,2)'. False on two independent counts. (i) alpha_1 was carved out of gamma_1, which contains only direct products pi_1 x pi_2 preserving the H_1/H_2 split; automorphisms of M_(1,2) may move vertices between the two blocks and are simply absent from gamma_1, so alpha_1 can miss most of Aut(M_(1,2)). (ii) alpha_1 additionally requires mapping H-blocks onto G-blocks, which as noted in 0036 is incompatible with fixing M_(1,2). Nothing is proved; the identification of alpha_1 with Aut(M_(1,2)) is asserted. The bound |alpha_1| < n^9 does follow from 0032.
0040-0041 Case 1 is a non sequitur: |alpha_1| = 1 says exactly one element of gamma_1 meets the constraints; it does not imply 'for each pi_1 in beta_1 there is only one pi_2 in beta_2'. The stated cardinality n^2 for gamma_1 also contradicts the n^9 (or n^6) bound just derived.
0046 Case 2 asserts that from |alpha_1| > 1 one 'would be able to construct a generating set S_1 of Aut(M_(1,2))' with <S_1> = Aut(M_(1,2)). Unjustified and false in general: a subset of split-preserving permutations generates at most a subgroup of the split-preserving automorphisms. The follow-on 'if pi_a in Aut(H) acts on vertices of H_1 ∪ H_2 then pi_a in <S_1>' inherits that gap. The appeal to Theorem 7 of [3] (obtaining Aut from an intersection of a permutation group with a direct product of symmetric groups) does not supply this - that intersection problem is itself GI-hard and no polynomial procedure for it is given.
0048 Step 3: 'construct S_1 from alpha_1 in polynomial time' cites [3] Thm 9, but Schreier-Sims-type constructions need the group (or a generating set) as input, and alpha_1 is neither. The size bound |S_1| <= log(n!) is the standard log_2 |group| bound and is fine in itself.
0049 'S_1 generates Aut(H_1 ∪ H_2)' - false for the reasons in 0038/0046, and inconsistent with 0036's requirement that the same permutations carry H onto G.
0052 Step 4 iterates using beta_3, S_1 and M_(2,3). Two fresh defects: M_(2,3) involves only H_2, H_3 and ignores the edges R_(1,3), so the object being stabilized is not H_1 ∪ H_2 ∪ H_3; and Aut of a union is not generated by direct products of automorphisms of its parts, so the conclusion that S_2 generates Aut(H_1 ∪ H_2 ∪ H_3) does not follow. |S_2| <= log(n!) would hold for a correctly built generating set but is moot.
0056 Step 5 propagates the same unjustified inductive step to S_(x-1) and concludes <S_(x-1)> = Aut(H); the induction rests entirely on the broken base and inductive steps 0038-0052, so it fails. It also silently assumes the per-iteration candidate sets stay polynomially bounded, which is never shown.
0058 Assumes the oracle also supplies permutation sets for G. This strengthens the hypothesis of the Claim (which posits only beta_i witnessing G_i ~ H_i), so even a correct argument here would prove a different statement.
0061 'Once we generate generating sets of G, H, we can decide isomorphism between them [1]' - false as stated. Knowing generating sets of Aut(G) and of Aut(H) separately does not decide G ~ H; the Mathon/Luks equivalence is a Turing reduction that computes automorphisms of the disjoint union G ∪ H and looks for one exchanging the two components. No such construction is performed.
0065-0073 Reference list; not mathematical steps.
0079 Closing remark; no content.
Overall: the proof never establishes that the local permutation sets can be glued, and its central identification of a set of split-preserving direct products with a full automorphism group (0038) is false, so the O((x*beta)^c) bound is not proved.
